message.content: {"caption":"A two-stage agent workflow connects case-based planning and memory with MCP-mediated tool execution.","description":"The figure is a left-to-right workflow diagram with a teal Stage 1, “Case-Based Planning,” and a yellow Stage 2, “Tool-based Execution.” In Stage 1, the Case Memory box contains stored case notation, an “Online updating θ” component and “Replay Buffer,” a yellow “Read” component labeled with a retrieval-policy expression, and a cylinder labeled “Case Bank.” A state labeled s_t enters Read from the left, and the case-bank connection is labeled M_t. Read connects downward to the LLM Planner; a “Write(s_t, a_t, r_t, M_t)” connection indicates writing information back to memory. The LLM Planner also receives the user query from below and sends an “Answer” leftward out of the diagram. The User Query card reads: “I was watching this YouTube video ... on June ... tell me the character’s first name.” The Decomposed Plan card lists: 1. Identify the YouTube ID of the video; 2. Examine the thumbnail of the video; 3. Identify the first name in thumbnail. The planner sends “Planning/Replanning” toward a numbered subtask list, accompanied by a circular repeat-arrows symbol. Subtask Memory holds entries “(Subtask 1, Result 1),” “(Subtask 2, Result 2),” an ellipsis, and “(Subtask n, Result n).” A “Store” connection carries the numbered subtasks into this memory, and a return connection labeled “Return, if all subtasks done” points back toward the planner. A “Subtask” connection goes right from the subtask-memory side to the LLM Executor; a “Result” connection returns left from the executor toward subtask memory. In Stage 2, Tool Memory contains records “(Tool 1, Arg 1, Result 1),” “(Tool 2, Arg 2, Result 2),” an ellipsis, and “(Tool k, Arg k, Result k).” The executor connects upward to this memory through separate “Read” and “Store” connections. The MCP protocol box lists “Unified Interface,” “Safety and Scaling,” and “Client-Server Arch.” The Tool Register shows a function-definition template with fields for type, function, name, description, and parameters. A downward connection labeled “Init” leads from the register to the MCP Server. The LLM Executor sends “Tool Args” toward the server and receives “Tool Description” and “Result” connections back; a circular repeat-arrows symbol is shown beside this interaction. From the MCP Server, branching lines connect down to six external-tool icons labeled Search, Crawl, Video, Image, Code, Math, and Doc. The icons depict the corresponding tool categories. No plotted data, checks, or crosses appear.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
